appraisal_events.evidence: Robert sees and returns the narrator's deliberate salute but does not stop, offering only "sa main levée au bord de son képi, comme il eût répondu à un soldat qu'il n'eût pas connu," with no smile and no change of expression.
appraisal_events.explanation: Instead of the recognition and warmth the narrator seeks, Robert answers with a purely formal military gesture, as if to a stranger, leaving the narrator unable even to say goodbye.

status_effects.explanation: In that moment he is treated with the same impersonal formality Robert would show an unknown soldier, momentarily shut out of the intimacy their friendship had established.
Left "désolé" at being unable to say goodbye, the narrator visibly suffers the withholding of the acknowledgment he sought.

ambiguities: It is left unclear whether Robert's impersonal salute reflects a genuine failure to recognize the narrator or a deliberate formality maintained because he was not alone and was on duty; the passage does not resolve this, so no corresponding diminishment is scored for Robert himself.
